summary.text: Age-related appeals are not accepted. If you narrowly missed the citizenship date, contact the Appeals Panel to appeal.

steps.name: Check your birth date
steps.text: If you were born after 31 Dec 1949, you cannot appeal. The Panel considers citizenship-related appeals only.

items: If you were born after 31 Dec 1949, no appeal will be received.
The Panel considers appeals about citizenship only.

about.text: The age criterion applies to everyone, so the Panel does not make exceptions for age.

steps.name: Contact the Appeals Panel
steps.text: If you narrowly missed the citizenship date of 31 Dec 1986 and feel you meet the criteria, call 1800-2222-888 or email contactus@pioneers.gov.sg with your NRIC number to appeal.

items: If you marginally missed the citizenship date of 31 Dec 1986 and feel you meet the criteria, contact the Panel.
Call 1800-2222-888 or email contactus@pioneers.gov.sg with your NRIC number.
If you are appealing for a relative, get their consent first.

about.text: The Panel considers whether you obtained citizenship shortly after 1986, and also looks at your time in Singapore, contribution to society and efforts to sink roots here.

quotes.text: Hence, as provided under the Pioneer Generation Fund Act, the Panel decided that it would only consider appeals relating to the citizenship criterion.
If you were born after 31 Dec 1949, please note that no appeals will be received.

If you marginally missed the citizenship date of 31 Dec 1986 and you feel that you meet the criteria, please contact us at 1800-2222-888 or contactus@pioneers.gov.sg with your NRIC number to file an appeal.

Whatever the age set, there will always be those who marginally fall short of it. It would therefore not be feasible or fair to allow age-related appeals without extending the new age criterion to all Singaporeans.

For citizenship-related appeals, the Panel considers whether the person had obtained Singapore citizenship shortly after 1986 – the year set as the citizenship cut-off date for eligibility of the Pioneer Generation Package. In addition, it looks at factors such as whether he or she had been in Singapore since the early years of independence, contributed to our society, and had demonstrated clear efforts to sink roots in Singapore.
